title: Wasted Wind and Solar Power Could Run Factories and Data Centers
summary: As the scale and reach of variable renewable energies expand around the world, more and more clean energy is being produced. However, more and more of that clean energy is also going to waste. In order to balance energy supply and demand, electric utilities rely on a process called curtailment, where they deliberately reduce the amount of energy produced by solar and wind farms in order to not overwhelm the energy grid. But a new MIT study asks: what if that excess clean energy could be used to power some of the United States’ dirtiest sectors?…
body: Haley Zaremba is an energy journalist and researcher with more than a decade of professional experience covering global energy systems, land and natural resources, and… As the scale and reach of variable renewable energies expand around the world, more and more clean energy is being produced. However, more and more of that clean energy is also going to waste. In order to balance energy supply and demand, electric utilities rely on a process called curtailment, where they deliberately reduce the amount of energy produced by solar and wind farms in order to not overwhelm the energy grid. But a new MIT study asks: what if that excess clean energy could be used to power some of the United States’ dirtiest sectors? While solar and wind energies are essential to achieving decarbonization goals and avoiding the worst impacts of climate change, their intermittency introduces new challenges and complexity to energy markets and infrastructure. The production patterns of these renewable energy sources are often at odds with demand patterns. The sun is setting on solar farms just as families are returning home and firing up their appliances. And during the day, when production is at its highest, demand slumps. One of the most key approaches to this problem is energy storage , which can hold onto excess energy produced at peak hours and release it back onto the grid when demand outstrips supply. However, the energy storage sector is still in its infancy and battery storage can only hold onto energy for about four hours at a time. Long-term energy solutions, while very promising, are still in research and development stages and are not commercially viable or scalable. It would therefore be most efficient to divert that excess energy production to where it actually is needed – manufacturing and data centers. The idea of diverting clean energy to where it’s needed isn’t new, but it has lacked the infrastructure and data to reliably be carried out. “The key challenge is how to harness that extra energy, sending it to places where demand is high, or storing it for still and sunless days,” reads a Zenobe report . “At present, we don’t have sufficient network infrastructure to achieve this. This means that high levels of renewable generation put pressure on the grid, and sometimes even risk overloading it. At such times, the ESO safeguards the grid by paying generators to stop producing electricity,” Zenobe goes on to say. “This drives up bills for consumers, and wastes precious renewable energy.” But it’s not just an issue of infrastructure. It’s also an issue of being able to reliably model when and where that excess energy will be available in order to design systems around it. A new study from MIT and Georgia Tech, published this week in the energy-focused scientific journal Joule , seeks to answer that need. The study models the future of wind and solar growth the the United States. Specifically, the study looks at the amount of excess energy to be produced as the domestic renewable sector continues to develop, and the patterns of when that excess energy will be produced. “The researchers’ model reveals when excess electricity will likely be available,” explains a recent article from MIT News. “It shows that periods of excess will generally occur in the spring and fall and usually persist for several hours at a time.” These models are based on a point in the future clean energy development wherein 80 percent of the electricity supplied to United States consumers is coming from solar and wind power. At that time, their model projects that the renewable energy sector will produce 10 percent more energy than the grid can use or store. This means that energy will go to waste if we don’t plan accordingly. “In this era where there is a need for additional electricity, where demands are growing to support data centers and other end users, we wanted to understand what this excess electricity will potentially look like so we can design processes to b

title: Brent Nears $100 as Supply Risks Challenge Oil Glut Forecasts - Dosya Haber
body: ICE Brent climbed to $96 a barrel after attacks on Saudi refineries and tighter physical supplies rattled energy markets. NEW YORK — Crude oil prices are on track to snap a three-week losing streak as ICE Brent climbed to $96 per barrel , challenging widespread market expectations of an impending global supply glut. With Dated Brent approaching $100 per barrel , traders returning from the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday slowdown are reassessing physical supply risks. The latest rally follows recurring Houthi strikes targeting major Saudi Arabian energy facilities, including the Jizan and Ras Tanura refineries. Beyond security disruptions in the Middle East, physical crude markets are showing signs of strain due to faltering Norwegian production and lower-than-expected Iraqi exports. Analysts note that once full trading volume resumes next week, triple-digit oil prices could return to the table. Market volatility coincides with growing friction inside OPEC+. According to Reuters, the Trump administration urged founding OPEC members Iraq and Venezuela to consider leaving the cartel and blocked Caracas from paying its membership dues, though Saudi intervention reportedly eased U.S. Pressure on Venezuela. Ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting, Iraq rejected a capacity assessment by DeGolyer and MacNaughton that placed its output potential just under 5 million barrels per day , insisting it can pump 5.2 million barrels per day . Despite internal disputes over capacity baselines, OPEC+ members have reached an in-principle agreement to keep their collective 31.01 million barrels per day production target unchanged for the first quarter of 2027 . Meanwhile, in natural gas markets, Australia's parliament passed legislation requiring east coast LNG exporters to reserve up to 20% of output for domestic use starting in 2028 .

Other Fed policymakers have also maintained similar views, suggesting that they are unlikely to tolerate elevated inflation simply because financial markets are struggling. title: Bitcoin's Macro Trend Shifts in 2026 Amid Rising US Interest Rate Expectations - KuCoin
body: Bitcoin entered 2026 with expectations of cheaper borrowing, improving liquidity, and a more supportive economic environment. As the year approaches its end, investors are preparing for a very different 2027. Financial markets now expect US interest rates to reach 4.50%–4.75% by June 2027. According to BloFin Research , that could extend the pressure on Bitcoin for another six months. However, understanding how these expectations changed throughout 2026 offers an important clue about when Bitcoin’s recovery could begin. At the beginning of 2026, investors anticipated one or two interest rate cuts. Inflation was moderating in the services sector, while slowing job growth supported the case for cheaper borrowing. The Middle East conflict in late February changed that outlook. Rising energy and transportation costs threatened to push inflation higher across the economy. By late March, expectations of rate cuts had largely disappeared. Then came another complication: the US labor market remained resilient. Unemployment stayed between 4.1% and 4.3% over the spring and summer, giving the Federal Reserve greater flexibility to fight inflation. The evolution of the Fed’s own economic projections illustrates how dramatically the outlook changed. November brought a particularly aggressive shift in market expectations. Investors now anticipate three additional quarter-point rate increases by June 2027, including December’s expected hike. Higher interest rates make government bonds and other interest-bearing investments more attractive while increasing the cost of borrowing. This reduces the incentive to take risks on assets such as Bitcoin. The November repricing contributed to sharp declines across both Bitcoin and gold, undermining the earlier case that Bitcoin’s bear market was over. Bitcoin’s turning point could arrive well before interest rates begin falling. Annual core PCE inflation reached 3.3%, exceeding expectations. Yet monthly core inflation slowed from 0.32% to 0.29%, while inflation-adjusted consumer spending remained flat. Bitcoin subsequently recovered from its intraday lows as Treasury yields fell. This market reaction matters because investors already expect substantial monetary tightening. Evidence that fewer rate hikes may be necessary could therefore support a recovery. Throughout 2027, investors should closely monitor inflation , employment figures and changes in Fed rate expectations. Persistent inflation could prolong Bitcoin’s downturn. A sustained moderation in inflation or weaker economic demand could bring relief sooner, although a severe economic slowdown would introduce its own risks. One of the earliest macroeconomic signals of Bitcoin’s recovery in 2027 could be a sustained decline in expectations for further interest rate hikes. title: This Analyst Sees A 47% Downside For SPCX Stock – Firm Flags Heavy AI Spending And Customer Concentration Risks - Stocktwits
body: SpaceX (SPCX) was in the spotlight on Monday after Phillip Securities reiterated its bearish stance, warning that the revenue which pushed its artificial intelligence business into profit may not be durable. Phillip Securities reiterated a ‘Sell’ rating and price target of $75 for SpaceX, implying a near 47% downside from current levels, according to a report by Investing.com The brokerage noted that SpaceX’s cloud customers pay monthly fees and can terminate their contracts with 90 days’ notice. A rerating of the stock’s valuation would require these agreements to be converted into longer-term commitments. Customer concentration is another risk, it says. One AI customer generated 19.5% of SpaceX’s second-quarter revenue, up from less than 10% a year earlier. Meanwhile, SpaceX recorded a $542 million operating loss, while capital spending was 2.4 times its revenue. The firm initiated coverage of SpaceX last month, stating that it expects the company to remain unprofitable and burn cash through at least 2030. SpaceX’s second-quarter revenue jumped 92% to $7.81 billion, beating Wall Street’s $6.82 billion estimate, according to Fiscal.ai. Starlink revenue rose 67%, launch sales grew 29%, and AI revenue surged 247%. It reported a loss of $0.09 per share. Despite Phillip Securities’ caution, SpaceX continues to receive strong support across Wall Street. Morgan Stanley has a $300 price target, while its $600 bull case assumes faster progress across AI, Starship and orbital computing. JPMorgan recently raised its SpaceX price target to $240 from $225 and maintained an ‘Overweight’ rating, citing the company’s deep vertical integration and the rapid pace of change in AI, according to The Fly. Overall, the stock has a consensus 12-month price target of $227, according to Koyfin. Twenty-eight of the 35 analysts covering the stock have a ‘Buy’ rating, five have a ‘Hold’ rating, and two have a ‘Sell’ rating. Separately, regulatory filings on Friday showed that Harvard Management held a $2.2 billion stake in SpaceX, while Nvidia (NVDA) disclosed ownership of 122.8 million shares worth around $21 billion. title: DELL Stock Shrugs Off Market Slump As Analysts See ‘Surging’ AI Demand After 'Blowout' Q2 Beat - Stocktwits
body: Dell Technologies (DELL) shares surged in early morning trade on Wednesday after the company reported a second quarter earnings beat and raised its full-year outlook, prompting a wave of price-target hikes from Wall Street. In a note to investors cited by TheFly, Citi called Dell’s second quarter (Q2) results a “clear beat” amid “surging” demand, while Morgan Stanley said “blowout” quarters like Q2 should continue for Dell as long as supply is short and execution is strong. DELL stock rose nearly 8% in pre-market and was among the top-trending tickers on Stocktwits at the time of writing, outperforming the broader market, which trended lower on escalating tensions in the Middle East and inflation worries. The Nasdaq-100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1 (QQQ) edged around 0.4% lower in pre-market trade, while the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust traded flat. BofA raised its price target on Dell to $600 from $505 and maintained a ‘Buy’ rating, pointing to demand that “continues to outpace supply.” The firm also raised its fiscal 2027 revenue and earnings estimates after Dell's AI server revenue, orders and backlog came in well above its expectations. Melius Research delivered the most aggressive target shown in the analyst updates, raising its price target to $735 from $650 while maintaining a ‘Buy’ rating, followed by JPMorgan, which raised its price target to $635 from $565 and called the results “another robust quarter.” JPMorgan pointed to “continued AI momentum,” an increasingly durable IT infrastructure refresh, and PC demand that has proven more resilient than expected. Barclays also flagged Dell's traditional server and networking business, which grew 122% year over year in the quarter. The firm said AI is driving incremental demand across data-center infrastructure. The firm lifted its target to $603 from $550 and maintained an ‘Overweight’ rating on Dell shares. Meanwhile, Piper Sandler raised its target to $558 from $497, citing customer reallocations of budgets toward IT and workload modernization. The firm also said demand continues to outstrip supply, while on-premise and edge infrastructure offers attractive economics for enterprise AI inference. Morgan Stanley raised its target to $499 from $434 but kept an ‘Equal Weight’ rating. The firm said the results show companies are investing heavily in AI across cloud, hybrid and on-premise environments, while warning about the durability of Dell's ISG pricing and margin capture. Piper Sandler similarly noted some investor pushback over how much of Dell's gains are coming from pricing versus volume. Dell reported record quarterly revenue of about $47 billion, up 58% year over year, and ahead of Wall Street’s estimate of $46.7 billion. AI-optimized server revenue reached $16.4 billion. Dell also booked a record $60.9 billion in AI server orders and ended the quarter with a $95 billion backlog. The Texas-based laptop and AI server maker projected annual revenue of around $192 billion for the fiscal year ending in January 2027. The new forecast represents a $25 billion increase from its previous target of $167 billion set in May. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Dell rose to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ territory over the past day, while chatter increased to ‘extremely high’ from ‘high’ levels. One retail trader on the platform cited weakness in technicals, forecasting that DELL stock may fall once the market opens. Others were more bullish, with one predicting that DELL stock could cross $500 at market open. DELL stock has gained over 230% this year and more than 250% in the last 12 months. title: AMD, Intel, Broadcom rally in premarket trading Friday as AI stocks rebound - TradingView
body: Chip stocks were rallying in premarket trading on Friday as investors bought the dip following the Thanksgiving holiday. Intel and AMD gained roughly 4% and Broadcom jumped 3% in early premarket trading at 6:45 AM ET. All three stocks, alongside major names in the artificial intelligence trade, have been under pressure in recent weeks, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq briefly entering bear-market territory in the previous session. Intel had shed 0.6% on Wednesday to close at $54.47, AMD had lost 1.75% to $406 while Broadcom stayed almost flat at $300.86. The broader market was also looking set to jump, with futures linked to all three major indexes rising ahead of the shortened trading session to close the week. However, with fundamental questions around the sustainability of the AI trade still looming, analysts are unsure whether the rebound will be durable. "The recovery in stocks seems technical. The questions that caused the market panic are still unanswered," Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB, told Reuters. "If these gains can be sustained on Friday, it would suggest that enthusiasm for the AI trade is back." There have nevertheless been some positive developments for individual chipmakers that could help support sentiment. Intel has secured two important customer developments that could support its manufacturing ambitions. CEO Lip-Bu Tan announced Thursday that the company had signed its first external customer for its advanced 18A-P chip manufacturing process. Intel has not disclosed the customer's identity, but the agreement marks progress in its effort to compete with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Separately, Microsoft became the first publicly named customer for Intel Foundry's EMIB advanced packaging technology, which will be used for Microsoft's Azure first-party silicon. AMD has also made progress in its efforts to secure a larger share of the AI infrastructure market even as it struggles with allegations of links with blacklisted Chinese firms. On November 16, AI infrastructure provider TensorWave announced a six-year agreement with OpenAI to supply 457 megawatts of dedicated computing capacity across multiple US data-center locations. AMD has also completed its acquisitions of AI research startup World Labs, led by Fei-Fei Li, and specialised inference-chip developer Taalas. China’s extension of the pause in controls on critical minerals till January is another good news for chipmakers, even though it is only a short-term relief. Minerals like gallium and germanium are critical inputs in semiconductor manufacturing. Analysts also remain bullish on the stock with TipRanks data showing 27 out of 30 analysts keeping a 'buy' rating and three suggesting 'hold'. Broadcom has also faced significant pressure recently and investors chipped in on Friday to buy the stock, pushing it up before the opening bell. It recently secured a significant development in its AI business through a financing arrangement involving some of Wall Street's biggest financial institutions. Bank of America, Blackstone, Citi and Morgan Stanley announced a $63 billion financing structure in October to fund the purchase of Broadcom's custom AI accelerators and networking equipment for Anthropic. Several Wall Street firms, including StoneX, UBS, and Rosenblatt have reiterated their Buy ratings on Broadcom, but some like Rothschild Redburn have also downgraded the stock with concerns over AI financing and the sustainability of earnings. Broadcom is scheduled to report its fourth-quarter and full-year 2026 financial results on December 9, giving investors another opportunity to assess whether its AI business can sustain growth despite recent concerns about chip demand. title: NBIS, IREN, MRVL Stocks Rally: Nvidia Vows To Keep AI Financing Flywheel Turning, But ‘Disciplined’ – Analyst Calls Neoclouds Its ‘Biggest Sustained Bet’ - Stocktwits
body: Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) on Tuesday said it will continue supporting the AI infrastructure buildout through investments and credit guarantees, albeit with a “selective” and “disciplined” approach, easing a key concern AI investors had after former CEO Jensen Huang's exit. Nvidia’s interim CEO Colette Kress highlighted neocloud operators as an important part of the AI chain and its continued support, but clarified that credit backstops activate only if partners can build and deliver the computing infrastructure. Neocloud, AI infrastructure, and chip stocks rallied on the disclosures, buoyed by Nvidia’s strong quarterly results and outlook. Nebius (NBIS) and IREN ltd. (IREN) rose over 10% in overnight trading late Tuesday, while CoreWeave (CRWV) gained 9%. Marvell Technology (MRVL) gained 5.7% and Arista Networks (ANET) rose 3.7%. Chip heavyweights Intel (INTC), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Micron (MU) and Broadcom (AVGO) rose 2.7% to 4.7%, pushing the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) 3.8% higher. "Neoclouds remain an increasingly important part of the global AI infrastructure ecosystem, providing additional customers with access to Nvidia compute and expanding the reach of our platform,” Kress said on the analyst call. “We have supported the development of this ecosystem, and we will continue to be disciplined and selective in our support." Nvidia has become a de facto financier of AI infrastructure, partnering with and investing in dozens of companies. Huang played a central role in these deals, and his departure fueled concerns that Nvidia might scale back its support. "As we advance this work, we remain thoughtful in how we participate and disciplined in how we commit capital. We are proud of the role that we have played so far in supporting the ecosystem,” Kress said. “As the market matures and additional sources of capital become available, we are rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments and guarantees," Kress said. Nvidia disclosed $32 billion in neocloud commitments, down from $36 billion in Q2, and $118 billion in total guarantees. The chipmaker reported $390 billion committed toward future supply and capacity, up from $279 billion a quarter ago. Nvidia said the uptick was “primarily related to the multiyear procurement of memory supply,” the company said. “Beyond its impressive, consensus-beating revenue growth and profitability, Nvidia’s quarterly earnings also highlight its expanding role as a major AI creditor and investor,” Wharton professor Mohamed A. El-Erian said in an X post . Hedge fund manager Eric Jackson said Nvidia’s push in AI infrastructure was the earnings’ highlight: “When asked about future financing priorities, Colette Kress singled out the physical infrastructure needed to house AI compute.” The Futurum Group CEO Daniel Newman said neocloud commitments are “critical” to Nvidia’s growth. “The Neoclouds aren’t a nice to have for $NVDA. It’s the biggest sustained bet it has on creating an ecosystem of NVIDIA powered hyperscalers that won’t look to build competitive or meaningfully augment with custom silicon.” Nvidia’s third-quarter revenue more than doubled to $115.8 billion, beating expectations of $109.3 billion. Sales from the all-important data center segment rose 110% to $107.6 billion, also higher than targets. Nvidia forecast $130 billion in revenue for the current quarter, about 4% higher than Wall Street estimates according to The Wall Street Journal. Kress said the company was raising its forecast revenue growth for fiscal 2028 from 70% to 75%. Last week, the company cut ties with Huang, its 63-year-old co-founder, following a scandal involving multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman who is alleged to be a Chinese spy. On a call with analysts, Harvey C. Jones, the newly appointed chairman of the board, said Nvidia wasn’t considering reinstating Huang as CEO. title: SpaceX Stock Could Nearly Double — Analyst Says Nvidia Rubin Chips Could Fuel One-Year Payback - Stocktwits
body: Shares of SpaceX (SPCX) could nearly double as its Nvidia-powered AI expansion opens up a larger revenue opportunity, Oppenheimer says. SPCX stock fell 1% on Wednesday to $140.71, logging its second consecutive session in the red. Oppenheimer raised its SpaceX price target to $280 from $250, implying a 99% upside from current levels, and maintained its ‘Outperform’ rating. The firm identified SpaceX’s vertically integrated AI platform as a key differentiator. According to a report on Investing.com, the research firm said that the company owns valuable data, has access to substantial capital and Nvidia GPUs, and can build infrastructure rapidly. Oppenheimer said new Nvidia Rubin chips could pay for themselves in one year amid strong AI compute demand and pricing. SpaceX could retain 100% of the revenue generated through Cursor and Grok or capture around 50% when acting as an AI infrastructure wholesaler, the firm said. The Cursor acquisition has also strengthened SpaceX’s agentic coding data and reasoning capabilities, benefiting Grok Bot and Grok 4.6, with further improvements expected in Grok 5.0. Oppenheimer said AI usage and productivity are running ahead of expectations, although infrastructure remains the biggest bottleneck. The firm raised its long-term revenue estimates by about 10% on stronger compute pricing, compounding to 20% over time when combined with higher capex. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Nvidia recently detailed a space-optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 system, targeting initial launches in the fourth quarter of 2027 and significant scaling in 2028. SpaceX’s first-gen Starmind AI1 satellite is designed around an orbital configuration of 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs. SpaceX also adopted standalone Vera CPUs for Grok’s agentic workloads on Earth, making Nvidia’s architecture the backbone of both its terrestrial Colossus-scale builds and orbital computing network. Deepwater’s Gene Munster estimated that SpaceX already contributes nearly $5 billion, or 5%, of Nvidia’s quarterly revenue, up from 3%. He said Nvidia may increasingly view SpaceX as a hyperscaler peer given its massive compute plans. Nvidia has also disclosed an ownership stake in SpaceX. SpaceX revealed the scale of its AI ambitions during its first public earnings call last month. The company expects to exceed 2 GW of computing capacity by the end of 2026 and move closer to 10 GW than 5 GW by the end of 2027. Its broader power-and-cooling pipeline totals 20 GW. Musk said SpaceX has committed to using Nvidia GPUs exclusively “because they are the best.” He also expects the company to receive a significant percentage of Nvidia’s GPU production next year. Melius Research estimated that even 2 GW of SpaceX’s planned buildout could generate $100 billion in incremental revenue for Nvidia. Meanwhile, the capital required for SpaceX’s 2027 expansion has been estimated at between $300 billion and $500 billion. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for SpaceX has been ‘bearish’ over the past week amid a 16% decline in 24-hour message volumes. One bullish user said , “$SPCX Oppenheimer target is ridiculous” Another user noted , “$SPCX increased price targets and new contracts everyday, and this thing can barely clear the ipo price” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. title: Alphabet's AI Spending Under the Microscope as Credit Hedges Set Records - ad-hoc-news.de
body: Investors in Alphabet are being pushed to look past the headlines this week. A record reading in the credit-default swap market, an unconfirmed report of trimmed chip orders and a pair of legal developments have all landed within days of each other — and each one, on closer inspection, says less about Alphabet's prospects than the questions it raises about the return on its artificial intelligence spending. The cost of insuring against an Alphabet default climbed to a record on Wednesday for five-year contracts, according to Reuters, which noted that premiums for Oracle, SpaceX and CoreWeave also touched all-time highs. The agency tied the moves to investor unease over AI outlays and how they are financed. That concern has been building. Axios reported on 23 November that analysts had not raised their forecasts for further investment by Alphabet and other large cloud providers after the earnings season — a break from a pattern of repeated upgrades to AI spending expectations. On Tuesday, Alphabet and other AI-linked stocks came under pressure as investors questioned whether returns would justify the heavy data-center buildout. The week's most eye-catching item was an unconfirmed media report suggesting Google could cut orders for custom AI chips for 2027 by roughly 20%. On its own, such a reduction would prove neither greater efficiency nor weaker demand. Order volume says nothing about how overall capital needs will develop, nor about the revenue Alphabet can wring from existing capacity. What matters for the stock is whether additional capital translates into additional earnings. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Alphabet? The unchanged analyst forecasts are a separate matter from any company decision. Axios reported on expectations, not on reduced investment budgets. A forecast that stops rising merely front-runs one more increase; it does not answer whether Alphabet can extract more from its AI investments. In the best case, Google needs fewer additional chips without any deterioration in its AI revenue outlook — a lower need for new silicon that sits comfortably alongside a better return. But that would require more than confirmation of a smaller order: Alphabet would also have to show the reduced need does not stem from weaker business prospects. A favorable scenario does not depend on a cut at all; even with spending still high, the company could demonstrate that extra capacity pays off. For investors, a statement on expected revenue relative to investment needs would carry more weight than any single order number. The counter-risk is that fewer orders signal softer demand while data-center expansion costs stay elevated. A purchasing cut would then offer scant offset to diminished revenue prospects — and even if the rumor never confirms, the risk remains that earnings fail to keep pace with the investment tempo. Financing sensitivity was on display in a Bloomberg Law report from 19 November: two energy prepayment deals totaling $3 billion were delayed amid weak investor demand and market volatility. Alphabet should still receive the funds, and the delay does not prove any cutback in AI investment. It does, however, explain why investors should watch the financing of individual projects alongside planned spending. The next concrete test would be a confirmation or denial of the reported 2027 orders. A confirmation alone would not settle which scenario applies — the reason would be decisive. Does Google need less additional capacity because it can use existing capacity better, or because it expects less business? A denial, meanwhile, would clear the rumor without answering whether AI revenue justifies the capital deployed. Alphabet at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. Alongside the AI debate, Alphabet has been active on several other fronts. On Friday it raised C$6 billion in a Canadian bond placement split across four tranches. Google also named Blue Origin on 2
